# Testament of Zebulun — 6
**Arbiter:** SOPHIA | **In council with:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA
**Source Manuscript:** Greek MS (Codex Cantabrigiensis) | **Section:** Testaments of the Twelve Patriarchs

---

1:1 The copy of the words of Zebulun, which he enjoined upon his sons before he died, in the hundred and fourteenth year of his life.
1:2 He said to them: Hearken to me, ye sons of Zebulun, attend to the words of your father.
1:3 I, Zebulun, was a good gift to my parents, for when I was born my father was increased in flocks and herds.
1:4 I am not conscious that I have sinned all my days, save in thought.
1:5 Nor do I remember that I have done any iniquity, except the sin of ignorance which I committed against Joseph; for I covenanted with my brethren not to tell my father what had been done to Joseph.
1:6 But I wept in secret many days because of him, for I feared my brethren, because they had all agreed that if any one should declare the secret, he should be slain.
1:7 But when they wished to kill him, I adjured them with many tears not to be guilty of this sin.

2:1 For Simeon and Gad came against Joseph to kill him. And he said to them with tears: Pity me, my brethren, have mercy upon the bowels of Jacob our father; lay not your hands upon me to shed innocent blood, for I have not sinned against you.
2:2 And if I have indeed sinned, chastise me with discipline, but lay not your hand upon me, for the sake of our father Jacob.
2:3 And as he spoke these words, weeping the while, I was unable to bear his lamentations, and I began also to weep, and my liver was poured out, and all the substance of my bowels was loosened.
2:4 And Joseph wept, and I wept with him; and the whole earth trembled at his voice.
2:5 And I stood up against my brethren and said: We will not slay him, but let us cast him into one of these dry pits, which our fathers dug and found no water in; for God forbid that we should destroy our brother.

3:1 And Simeon and Gad laid hold of Joseph to kill him; and I fell on my face before their feet, entreating them on behalf of Joseph.
3:2 And they pushed me aside, and Judah took him away from them, according to the word of our father Jacob.
3:3 And the Midianites came while Judah was absent, and drew up Joseph out of the pit, and sold him to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of gold.
3:4 And our brethren were ashamed and came and told our father that a wild beast had devoured Joseph; and they brought his coat and dipped it in the blood of a kid.

4:1 And after this I had great sorrow and grief, for I mourned over Joseph for a long time.
4:2 For from that day I took upon myself to be compassionate toward the poor and the sick and toward all who had need.
4:3 For I was moved to compassion for the crying of Joseph, and I purposed thenceforth to be compassionate toward all.
4:4 Neither was a hungry man unknown to me, nor a naked man; but I gave something from my goods to everyone who needed anything.
4:5 And now I say to you, my children: love the LORD with all your strength, and love one another in truth of heart.

5:1 For I perceive that through the hardness of your hearts all wickedness has its birth.
5:2 For he that is merciful and compassionate, even in poverty, shall be rich before God; but he that is rich in goods and hard of heart shall be poor before God.
5:3 For compassion is the gift of God; and he that hath it shall find mercy before God; but he that hath it not shall be desolate.
5:4 Have compassion therefore upon your neighbours, and be not unfeeling toward strangers; for wheresoever a man turns himself, the soul given to God in mercy shall always find a dwelling place.

6:1 For to what extent a man hath compassion on his neighbours, to that extent hath the LORD also upon him.
6:2 For when we went down into Egypt, Joseph bore no malice against us, but loved us as his own soul, and enriched us all.
6:3 Whom then should ye obey but God, who made heaven and earth and set the limits of the life of man?
6:4 Have compassion therefore upon your neighbours, and be not unfeeling toward strangers and the poor.
6:5 For wheresoever a man turns himself, the soul given to God in mercy shall always find a dwelling place.

7:1 And when Zebulun had said these things, he fell asleep in a good old age.
7:2 And his sons did as he had bidden them, and they carried him away and buried him in Hebron with his fathers.

---
*End of Testament of Zebulun*
